capabilities.target: Customer order refund issued through the payments processor, any order, any amount up to the order total

inputs.source: Support staff refund request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: "Process refund requests from support staff. Check the order, then issue the refund" places no limit on which orders, how many, or how large a refund can be beyond the order's own total.
"Use your judgment on partial refunds. Do not ask for confirmation" makes model judgment the only safeguard before an irreversible spend action and explicitly forbids adding a human check.
"Use your judgment on partial refunds" gives no criteria for what partial amount is appropriate for a given situation.

controls.name: Per-staff scoped credentials for refund and order actions
Daily/per-staff refund spend and rate cap
Refund destination bound to the order's original payment method of record
Tamper-evident per-request provenance log (staff identity, reason, order, amount)
Extended retention of staff refund requests for audit and dispute review

findings.title: Unbounded, unapproved refunds under a shared service account (any order, any amount)

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated staff member submits a refund request with no structured scope limit.
Agent reads order and payment details to check the order per prompt.md:1.
Agent issues the refund for any order, any amount up to the order total, via a shared service account, with no confirmation step (prompt.md:2).

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently constrains this path, so there is nothing further to decay. Watch for batch/bulk refund processing, delegation to other agents, or any further autonomy increase that would make the same unconstrained capability reachable at higher volume or lower scrutiny.

evidence.observation: "Process refund requests from support staff. Check the order, then issue the refund" places no limit on which orders or how large a refund can be, beyond the order total.
"Use your judgment on partial refunds. Do not ask for confirmation" explicitly removes any human confirmation step before an irreversible spend action.

"The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool" and "Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day," so any erroneous or malicious refund executes under a broad, unattributed credential and cannot later be undone.

recommendations.action: Require human approval (raw action review, showing the actual order, amount, and destination, not a summary) for refunds above a defined threshold.
Replace the shared service account with per-staff scoped credentials or an authenticated staff identity passed with each refund call, so privilege is least-privilege and attributable.
Add a daily or per-staff spend and rate cap on refunds issued by the agent, independent of the per-order total limit.
Constrain the refund payout destination to the original payment method recorded on the order, verified against the processor's own record rather than operator input.

findings.title: No attributable record of which staff member requested or justified each refund

forecast.watch_signal: No provenance control currently exists to decay. Watch for any lengthening of the agent's task horizon (batch or multi-day refund processing), further autonomy increases, or any shortening of the 7-day chat retention, none of which would change the finding but would confirm the gap persists or worsens.

evidence.observation: "The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why."
"The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days," so no alternate source of attribution survives past a week.
"Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day," so by the time a dispute or audit occurs, both the action and any chance to attribute it may be gone.

recommendations.action: Log the authenticated staff identity, timestamp, and stated reason with each refund request in a tamper-evident store the agent process cannot alter.
Retain the staff request record itself (not only the processor log) for a period sufficient for dispute and audit review, rather than deleting it after 7 days.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts state staff are 'SSO authenticated' but do not describe how the agent verifies session integrity or binds each request to a specific verified identity, so spoofing risk at the agent boundary cannot be assessed.
No information is given about deployment integrity controls, such as code signing or change control, for the agent's own configuration or prompt.
The agent has no egress capability in this design; order and payment data read via cap.order_read stays within agent processing for authorized staff and is never sent outside the trust boundary.
The artifacts do not describe the SSO identity provider's anti-spoofing or session hijacking protections, so whether a staff identity can be impersonated cannot be assessed here.
No information is provided about write protections or integrity guarantees on the payments processor's own transaction log.
The processor log is internal to the payments processor and the design includes no capability that reads it back out to a broader or external audience.
Availability of the payments processor's own log store is outside any capability this agent exercises; the agent cannot disable or exhaust it directly.

The chat transcript is explicitly ephemeral (deleted after 7 days) and is not relied on by the design as an integrity-bearing record, so tampering with it does not change what the agent or processor enforces.
The artifacts do not describe access controls on staff chat storage during its 7-day retention window, so disclosure risk during that window cannot be assessed.
No capability of the refund agent depends on the availability of this chat store to perform its core read or refund actions.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is high: a trusted, SSO-authenticated staff request reaches an irreversible spend capability (any order, any amount up to total) executed under a shared, unscoped service account, with the autonomy modifier applied because no step or runtime limit is declared and the design acts without any review (A4). Residual equals inherent because no control of any kind constrains the refund path today: the only artifact resembling a control is a prompt instruction that explicitly forbids confirmation, which is evidence of the weakness, not a control. A second finding captures a missing property: the processor log and the agent's own records cannot attribute any refund to the staff member who requested it, which is rated high under the internal-source baseline for an S3 sink. Forecast equals residual for both findings because there is nothing currently in place to decay further; the triggers considered (autonomy_increase, new_tool, longer_task_horizon) would not find an existing control to defeat. The single highest-value fix is adding a raw-action human approval gate, scoped per-staff credentials, and a tamper-evident provenance log on cap.issue_refund; none of these exist today, so they are recorded as missing_recommended controls rather than credited.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest or MCP/API configuration was provided for payments.issue_refund or orders.read; capability scope and credential handling are taken as described in the runtime notes, so confidence on exact enforcement is medium.

No information was provided about the SSO authentication mechanism's integrity or session security, so spoofing risk around staff identity could not be assessed and is recorded as not_assessed rather than scored.
